title: Introduce service ownership-claim propagation and KMS provenance gatekeeper
author: Priya Nandakumar
description: Motivation: Provide a defensible, auditable mapping from a service-level 'owner' claim to RBAC v2 role bindings and ensure KMS operations carry provenance tied to that owner. This change introduces a lightweight operator-side claim propagation path and a gatekeeper component that validates KMS requests against a provenance assertion before allowing key-wrap/unwrap operations. The goal is to improve incident forensics, reduce accidental cross-tenant KMS usage, and make region-pin decisions deterministic when an explicit owner claim is present. Summary of changes: 1) Add an ownership-claim extractor that reads service identity, explicit owner annotations, and fallback tenant metadata; normalizes claim format and emits a signed claim token used by downstream services. 2) RBAC v2 adapter: map ownership claim -> temporary derivative roles (read-only, crypto-op) and attach TTL-limited grants via the policy engine. 3) KMS provenance gatekeeper: middleware in the KMS proxy that validates the signed claim, checks residency constraints (region pin and locality policies), and stamps audit envelopes with origin provenance. 4) Audit enrichment: include owner.id, owner.role, and claim-hash in the immutable audit headers to help post-incident attribution and sampling-based retention. 5) Tests and docs: integration tests that simulate cross-region fallback, and a security doc with configuration knobs and recommended rollouts. Impact and rollout: default behavior is opt-in via a feature flag (auth.ownership_claims.enabled=false). During rollout we plan a shadow mode that logs provenance validation results (auth.ownership_claims.mode=shadow) and an automated Linear evaluation run (ENG-4281) for quality/regression checks. See linked Linear ticket ENG-4281 and security task SEC-102 for acceptance criteria. Checklist: - [x] Claim extractor implementation and unit tests - [x] RBAC v2 mapping plugin and policy templates - [x] KMS gatekeeper middleware and integration tests - [x] Audit header augmentation and retention guidance - [x] Feature flag + shadow mode - [x] Docs: docs/security/owner-claims.md - [x] End-to-end test in CI that verifies region-pin fallback when claim missing Known limitations: - Current implementation relies on the existing operator token exchange; we plan a follow-up to decouple operator token issuance (see linked_linear ENG-5120). - Edge case: services using legacy metadata that do not surface owner annotations will fallback to tenant metadata, which may be less precise for attribution. Operational notes: - Default audit retention for provenance-enriched events is increased to 90 days under the compliance package; operator can override via organizational policy. - KMS gatekeeper introduces an additional 6-12ms median p99 overhead for wrapped requests (measured in bench harness); included a perf knob to bypass validation for high-throughput internal-only keys. Documentation: docs/security/owner-claims.md explains configuration, rollout guide, and example policy templates for RBAC v2.
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial extractor and types; add RBAC v2 mapping plugin; implement KMS provenance validator + middleware; audit envelope stamping; add integration tests for region-pin behavior; docs and rollout notes.

release_notes: Adds operator-side service ownership claims, RBAC v2 mapping for ownership-derived roles, and a KMS provenance gatekeeper that validates claims and augments audit headers. Opt-in via feature flag; shadow mode available for staged rollout.
notes_for_sre: When enabling in production consider starting in shadow mode for 48-72 hours and inspect audit.provenance.* metrics. Watch KMS proxy p99 latency; perf knob available to skip validation for internal keys. Coordinate with infra for helm value auth.ownership_claims.enabled=true rollout.
security_considerations: Signed ownership claims rely on operator token integrity. Ensure operator token rotation policy is enforced and monitor audit.provenance.validation_failures. For regulated tenants, enable region pinning alongside claim validation to prevent cross-jurisdiction KMS usage.
testing_guidance: Use redwood/tests/integration/ownership_kms_test.go to run a three-node staging matrix: same-region, cross-region with explicit owner claim, cross-region without claim to validate fallback. CI includes a nightly bench job to track p99 latency impact.
